en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 3.5.
Saññojanagocchaka, Kusalattika (The Group on Fetters, Wholesome Triplet)
3.5.1.1. Section on the Wholesome and Unwholesome:
Root Condition, Not a Fetter Dependent on a wholesome state that is not a fetter, a wholesome state that is not a fetter arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition, one; in the case of object condition, one … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition, one. (Abbreviated.
[The same applies] in the section on co-nascence … pe … and in every instance of the section on inquiry.
Dependent on a fettering unwholesome state, a fettering unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a fettering unwholesome state, a non-fettering unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a fettering unwholesome state, both fettering unwholesome and non-fettering unwholesome states arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With root-cause condition: nine; with object condition: nine; with predominance condition: nine …pe… with non-disappearance condition:
nine. (Abbreviated. With not-root condition: three; with not-predominance condition: nine …pe… with not-kamma condition: three …pe… with not-dissociation condition: nine. (Abbreviated.
(The Chapter on Conascence …pe… and the Chapter on Association should also be expanded in the same manner as the Chapter on Dependence.)

An unwholesome state that is a fetter is related to an unwholesome state that is a fetter by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are three; under the object condition, nine;

under the predominance condition, nine … pe … under the decisive support and repetition conditions, nine; under the kamma condition, three; under the nutriment, faculty, and jhāna conditions, three; under the path, association, and non-disappearance conditions, nine. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, nine; with not-object condition, nine. (Abbreviated.
With root condition, not-object condition, three. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object condition, nine. (Abbreviated.)
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods were calculated for the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so too should they be calculated here. 3.5.1.2.
The Indeterminate Category: Root Condition (*Hetu*)
Dependent on a dissociated indeterminate state, there arises a dissociated indeterminate state by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition: one;
under object condition: one … pe … under non-disappearance condition: one. (Abbreviated.
[The same applies] throughout the section on co-nascence and the section on inquiry.
3.5.2. The Dyad of the Fettering (Saññojaniyaduka), within the Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika) 3.5.2.1.
The Section on the Wholesome and Unwholesome (Kusalākusalapada):
Root (Hetu)
Dependent on a wholesome state that is fetter-producing, a wholesome state that is fetter-producing arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is not fetter-producing, a wholesome state that is not fetter-producing arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are two; under object condition there are two. (Abbreviated.)
(Just as the transition from the *Lokiyaduka* follows the *Cūḷantaraduka*, so too should this be understood. The *Sahajātavāra* ... [and] the *Pañhāvāra* should be expanded in detail.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is conducive to fetters (*saññojaniya*), an unwholesome state conducive to fetters arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

(Abbreviated. Under the root condition there is one; under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*) there is one ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there is one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-arising as well... [and so on] ...in the section on questions as well, it is one in all cases. 3.5.2.2. Indeterminate Category:
Root (Hetu)
Dependent on a neutral state that is conducive to fetters, a neutral state conducive to fetters arises by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on a neutral state not conducive to fetters, a neutral state not conducive to fetters arises by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on a neutral state not conducive to fetters, a neutral state conducive to fetters arises by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on a non-fettering indeterminate state, there arise both fettering indeterminate and non-fettering indeterminate states by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a fettering indeterminate and a non-fettering indeterminate state, a fettering indeterminate state arises by way of root condition.
In the case of the root condition, there are five; in the object condition, two; in the predominance condition, five …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, five. (Abbreviated.
In the Lesser Intermediate Couplets, it is the same as in the Worldly Couplets. (The section on co-nascence should also be expanded …pe… as well as the section on association.
Root.
An indeterminate state that is fetter-producing is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate state that is fetter-producing.
An indeterminate state that is not fetter-producing is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate state that is not fetter-producing … three.
(Abbreviated. Under root there are four; under object, three; under predominance, four … pe … under non-disappearance, seven. (Abbreviated.)
An indeterminate state that is fetter-producing is a condition for an indeterminate state that is fetter-producing by way of object-condition,
conascence-condition, decisive-support-condition, prenascence-condition,
postnascence-condition, nutriment-condition, and faculty-condition.
Condition. (Abbreviated.
Seven [instances] for not-root; seven for not-object. (Abbreviated.
Four [instances] for not-object under the root-condition. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, three [answers] regarding the object. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive enumerations were calculated for the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet, so should they be calculated here.
3.5.3. The Dyad on Association with Fetters; The Wholesome Triplet.
3.5.3.1. Section on Wholesome and Unwholesome States:
Root Condition Dependent on a wholesome state dissociated from the fetters, there arises a wholesome state dissociated from the fetters by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to the root condition, one; with respect to the object condition, one ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, one.
(Abbreviated. (In the section on co-nascence as well ... pe ... in the section on inquiry as well, it is one in every instance.
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with fetters, an unwholesome state associated with fetters arises by way of the root condition ... three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with the fetters, an unwholesome state associated with the fetters arises by way of object-condition.

(Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are three; under object-condition there are five; under predominance-condition there is one ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition there are five. (Abbreviated; Positive. Negative.
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with the fetters, an unwholesome state associated with the fetters arises by way of the root condition:
dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt, delusion accompanied by doubt arises.
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with the fetters (*saññojana*), an unwholesome state dissociated from the fetters arises by way of the not-root condition (*na-hetupaccaya*):
dependent on the aggregates accompanied by restlessness, restlessness-accompanied delusion (*moha*) arises. (Abbreviated. Under the not-root condition there are two;

under the not-predominance condition there are five; under the not-prenascence condition there are five ... pe ... under the not-kamma condition there are three ... pe ... under the not-dissociation condition there are five. (Abbreviated; the negative [paccanīya] section.)
An unwholesome state associated with fetters is a condition for an unwholesome state associated with fetters by way of the root-condition (hetupaccaya).
An unwholesome state dissociated from fetters is a condition for an unwholesome state associated with fetters by way of the root-condition.
An unwholesome state associated with the fetters is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for an unwholesome state associated with the fetters... [nine].
An unwholesome state associated with the fetters is a condition, by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*), for an unwholesome state associated with the fetters. (Abbreviated.

[There are] two in the case of root-cause (*hetu*), nine in the case of object, one in the case of predominance, nine in the cases of immediate (*anantara*) and contiguity (*samanantara*), and [nine] in the cases of co-nascence (*sahajāta*) and mutuality (*aññamañña*).
With respect to dependence, there are five; with respect to decisive support and repetition, nine; with respect to kamma, three; with respect to nutriment, faculty, jhāna, and path, three;
with respect to association, five; with respect to presence, five … [and so on] … with respect to non-disappearance, five. (Abbreviated. 3.5.3.2. The Section on the Indeterminate (Abyākata-pada)
Dependent on a root-conditioned indeterminate state dissociated from the fetters, there arises an indeterminate state dissociated from the fetters by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under the root condition there is one; under the object condition there is one … pe … under the non-disappearance condition there is one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence …pe… and in the section on inquiry, it is the same in all cases. 3.5.4.
The Dyad of Fetters and the Fetterable; The Triplet of the Wholesome. 3.5.4.1.
The Section on the Wholesome and the Unwholesome.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is both fetter-inducing and not itself a fetter, there arises a wholesome state that is both fetter-inducing and not itself a fetter, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition: one; under object condition: one … pe … under non-disappearance condition: one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence, and likewise in the section on inquiry, it is the same in all cases.

Dependent on a state that is both a fetter and an object of fettering, which is unwholesome, there arises a state that is both a fetter and an object of fettering, which is unwholesome, by way of root condition... three. (Abbreviated.
Nine with respect to root, nine with respect to object, nine with respect to predominance... [and so on] ...nine with respect to non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)

Three by way of not-root; nine by way of not-predominance; nine by way of not-prenascence; nine by way of not-postnascence; nine by way of not-repetition; three by way of not-kamma; nine by way of not-resultant;
nine by way of not-dissociation. (Abbreviated. (The section on conascence ... [and] the section on association are similar to the section on dependence.
An unwholesome state that is both a fetter and a fetterable is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state that is both a fetter and a fetterable. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to root-condition: three; object-condition: nine; predominance-condition: nine ... [etc. ... decisive-support and repetition-conditions: nine; kamma, nutriment, faculty, and jhāna-conditions: three; path, association-conditions: nine ... [etc. ... non-disappearance-condition:
nine. (Abbreviated. With respect to not-root: nine; not-object: nine. (Abbreviated.
With root-condition, not-object: three. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, there are nine [answers] for the object [condition]. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods were calculated for the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet, so should they be calculated here. 3.5.4.2.
The Indeterminate Section.
Dependent on an indeterminate state that is both fetterable and not itself a fetter, there arises an indeterminate state that is both fetterable and not itself a fetter, by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root-condition: one; under object-condition: one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition: one. (Abbreviated.
[The same applies] in the section on co-nascence … pe … and in all instances of the section on inquiry: one.
3.5.5. The Dyad of the Fetter and that which is Associated with the Fetter; The Triad of the Wholesome;

The Root Condition. Dependent on an unwholesome state that is both a fetter and associated with a fetter, there arises an unwholesome state that is both a fetter and associated with a fetter, by way of the root condition... [three].

Dependent on unwholesome states that are associated with the fetters but are not themselves fetters, there arises an unwholesome state associated with the fetters but not itself a fetter, by way of root condition... [three].

Dependent on states that are both fetters and associated with the fetters and unwholesome, and dependent on states that are associated with the fetters but not themselves fetters and unwholesome, there arises an unwholesome state that is both a fetter and associated with the fetters.
Conditioned by root: three. (Abbreviated. Under root: nine; under object: nine; under predominance: nine ... pe ... under non-disappearance:

nine. (Abbreviated. Under not-root: three; under not-predominance: nine; under not-prenascence: nine; under not-postnascence: nine; under not-repetition: nine; under not-kamma: three; under not-resultant: nine; under not-dissociation: nine. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence and association should also be expanded in the same manner as the section on dependence.
An unwholesome state that is both a fetter and associated with a fetter is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state that is both a fetter and associated with a fetter.

(Abbreviated. [In the root-condition: three; [in the object-condition: nine; [in the predominance-condition: nine …pe… [in the decisive-support and repetition conditions: nine; [in the kamma, nutriment, faculty, jhāna conditions: three; [in the path, association conditions: nine …pe… [in the non-disappearance condition: nine. (Abbreviated.)
In the absence of the root condition, nine; in the absence of the object condition, nine; in the absence of the predominance condition, nine. (Abbreviated.
With the root condition, in the absence of the object condition, three. (Abbreviated.
In the absence of the root condition, in the presence of the object condition, nine. (Abbreviated.)
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods were calculated for the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so too should they be calculated here.
3.5.6. The Dyad of the Fetterless-yet-fetterable, the *Kusalattika*:
Root.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is dissociated from the fetters but is subject to the fetters, there arises a wholesome state dissociated from the fetters and subject to the fetters by way of root condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is dissociated from the fetters and not subject to the fetters, there arises a wholesome state dissociated from the fetters and not subject to the fetters by way of root condition. Under root condition there are two;
under object condition there are two ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are two. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the *Cūḷantaraduka*, it is similar to the *Lokiyaduka*. The "co-nascent" section ... [etc] ... and the "question" section should be expanded in all instances.

An unwholesome state that is dissociated from the fetters but is subject to fettering is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for an unwholesome state that is dissociated from the fetters and is subject to fettering.
(Abbreviated. One [condition] in the object. (In all cases, one; abbreviated.)

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the fetters, is subject to the fetters, and is indeterminate, there arises a state that is dissociated from the fetters, subject to the fetters, and indeterminate, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the fetters, is not subject to the fetters, and is indeterminate, there arises a state that is dissociated from the fetters, not subject to the fetters, and indeterminate, by way of root-condition. [Dependent on] a state that is dissociated from the fetters and not subject to the fetters...
Dependent on an indeterminate state dissociated from the fetters but conducive to fetters,

there arises an indeterminate state dissociated from the fetters and conducive to fetters by way of root condition. Dependent on an indeterminate state dissociated from the fetters and not conducive to fetters,

there arise both an indeterminate state dissociated from the fetters and conducive to fetters and an indeterminate state dissociated from the fetters and not conducive to fetters by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the fetters, is subject to the fetters, and is indeterminate,

and [dependent on] a state that is dissociated from the fetters, is not subject to the fetters, and is indeterminate, there arises a state that is dissociated from the fetters, is subject to the fetters, and is indeterminate, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition, there are five; in the object condition, two; in the predominance condition, five …pe… in the repetition condition, one; in the kamma condition, five; in the result condition, five …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, five. (Abbreviated. In the absence of the root condition, there is one;
in the absence of the object condition, three; in the absence of the predominance condition, two; in the absence of the prenascence condition, four;

in the absence of the postnascence condition, five; in the absence of the repetition condition, five; in the absence of the kamma condition, one; in the absence of the result condition, one; in the absence of the dissociation condition, two …pe… in the absence of the disappearance condition, three. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence … and on association are similar to the section on dependence.

A state that is dissociated from the fetters, is subject to the fetters, and is indeterminate is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is dissociated from the fetters, is subject to the fetters, and is indeterminate. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are four;
under object-condition, three; under predominance-condition, four; under proximity-condition, four … pe … under co-nascence-condition, [four].
Five [conditions] for mutuality, two for mutuality, seven for support, four for decisive support, two for prenascence and postnascence, one for repetition, [one for] kamma ...
pe ... four for the path, two for association, three for dissociation ... pe ...
seven for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
Seven by way of not-root; seven by way of not-object. (Abbreviated.
Four by way of root-condition, not-object. (Abbreviated.
Three by way of not-root-condition, object. (Abbreviated.)
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods were calculated for the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so too should they be calculated here.
The *Saññojanagocchaka-Kusalattika* is finished.
